title: Crime Scene Reconstruction
blurb: Rebuilds a scene in 3D from a handful of ordinary 2D photos — structure-from-motion with SIFT features, essential-matrix geometry and triangulation, the same technique behind photogrammetry tools like COLMAP.

steps.say: This rebuilds a scene in 3D from ordinary flat photos — structure from motion, the technique behind photogrammetry. You walk around a scene taking overlapping photos, and the shared detail between them is enough to recover both the scene's shape and where each photo was shot from.
Four rendered views of a simple scene — three blocks on a patterned floor — each shot from a different position, the way you'd circle a real one. Nothing here carries depth; it is all flat pixels.
Reconstruct. It finds SIFT keypoints in every photo, matches them across pairs, solves the camera geometry from those matches, and triangulates each matched point into 3D.

And the flat photos become a scene in space: a sparse point cloud of the blocks and floor, with a cone marking each recovered camera position. Drag to orbit it — the depth is real, solved purely from where features shifted between shots.

The honest limits: this is sparse structure-from-motion, not a dense model — matched keypoints only, no bundle adjustment and no camera calibration, so shape and scale are approximate. It is an educational demonstration of the real photogrammetry pipeline, not a forensic-grade measurement.
